creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Typing `muster upgrade` in a shell pane opens a new "⬆️ Upgrade Muster" tab and runs brew there,
when you'd expect it to run where you typed it. The tab exists so that brew outlives the app,
which the cask's `uninstall quit:` quits partway through (fccec5c7). But the calling pane is
already on the daemon and survives the quit just as well, so the new tab isn't needed for that.

Proposed: when called from a pane on this machine, the CLI asks the app for the upgrade command
(or its refusal), which `Upgrading.plan` already works out at launch, then runs it as its own
child process and exits with brew's status. Brew's output lands where you typed. An agent
calling it through its shell tool gets the output as that command's result, and its pane is
untouched.

Keep the separate tab where there is no suitable local shell: the "Upgrade muster" menu item,
and `muster upgrade` from an SSH pane, whose pane is on the wrong machine for brew.

Known gap, accepted: if brew ever stops for input (a sudo password), an agent's shell tool hangs.
Installs into /Applications don't normally ask.

`crates/muster-cli/tests/cli/upgrading.rs` changes from "opens a tab and prints its callsign" to
"runs the command and exits with its status"; update docs/cli/overview.md's Upgrading section.
title: Run muster upgrade in the calling pane, not a new tab
